routes.route: strengthen Dobson calibration and harmonize satellite ozone records to reduce instrument drift/coverage confounds
routes.reason: Directly targets the dominant bottleneck by building a reliable, intercalibrated ozone trend signal needed for causal attribution.

routes.route: advance atmospheric chemistry calculations and laboratory photochemistry for CFC chlorine cycles
routes.reason: Sharpens mechanistic predictions so observed trend patterns can be distinguished from measurement artifacts.

routes.route: defer large balloon/aircraft stratospheric CFC/ozone campaigns until the harmonized trend signal identifies a clear anomaly
routes.reason: In situ campaigns are expensive and currently cannot discriminate the predicted global trend from calibration noise, so waiting improves their targeting.

routes.route: negotiate voluntary international monitoring and staged control agreements
routes.reason: Monitoring cooperation is low-cost and builds an institutional framework that can act quickly if the causal evidence strengthens.

routes.route: evaluate application-specific substitute costs and transition pathways
routes.reason: Knowing where substitutes exist and what they cost reduces negotiation friction and prepares for eventual controls without assuming uniform feasibility.

bet.topRoute: strengthen Dobson calibration and harmonize satellite ozone records to reduce instrument drift/coverage confounds
bet.nextDiscriminatingTest: Cross-calibrate Dobson station and satellite ozone records against a common transfer standard, then test whether the measured altitude-latitude-season pattern of ozone changes matches the CFC chlorine-cycle fingerprint rather than uniform instrument drift.

bet.generalizationBoundary: This approach applies to global slow-onset atmospheric harms where the mechanism is credible but direct public validation is delayed and measurement noise can mimic the effect; it is not a template for acute, local, or directly observable environmental problems.
